- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid overestimating price rise.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period to avoid overcorrection.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67 bearish), model underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often overpredicts volatility — smooth forecast curve to avoid erratic swings.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., 3+ auctions in 30d), model tends to overreact — reduce forecast sensitivity to supply events by 15–20%.
- Mean reversion applies if price deviates >5% from 30d average — adjust forecast toward historical mean over 10–15d window.
- For bullish sentiment + negative supply net, model often fails to account for policy-induced volatility — add 1–3% downward buffer to prevent overconfidence.
